purpose: Drive an exploratory learning layer that asks the economically important question before exposing controls, then explains what changed and why.

leaps.title: LEAPS + safe asset
leaps.thesis: Use options for capital-efficient equity exposure while keeping residual capital in a safe or diversifying sleeve. The key question is whether the equity growth obtained is worth the price paid for long-dated convexity.
implicit_bets: Equity growth exceeds the option-pricing hurdle over long horizons
Long-dated implied volatility and downside skew are not persistently too expensive
The residual Treasury or safe-asset sleeve contributes enough diversification or carry to justify its capital allocation

questions.prompt: Why does this structure outperform 1x equities: more exposure, option convexity, or the Treasury sleeve?
questions.answer_hint: Compare delta-equivalent equity exposure and the residual sleeve before attributing excess return to structural efficiency.

questions.prompt: How expensive can long-dated options become before this strategy loses its advantage?
questions.answer_hint: A higher IV loading raises the price of each call. At a fixed premium budget the portfolio buys fewer contracts and usually less delta; distinguish that exposure effect from pure option-decay effects.

questions.prompt: Did a different maturity improve the strategy, or did it just buy a different amount of delta per premium dollar?
questions.answer_hint: The duration study found most apparent maturity advantages collapsed after matching delta; differences were generally smaller than one-vol-point option-pricing uncertainty.

questions.prompt: What happens when equities and long Treasuries fall together?
questions.answer_hint: Use 2022 and repeated-2022 style stress to separate equity-option risk from dependence on the diversifying sleeve.

questions.prompt: When a higher premium budget raises CAGR, did efficiency improve or did the portfolio simply take more equity risk?
questions.answer_hint: Compare median CAGR, p5 CAGR, drawdown probabilities, and mean delta together.

discoveries.headline: Shorter calls appear to outperform.
discoveries.notice: Check mean delta before calling this a maturity advantage.
discoveries.lesson: In the XND experiment, much of the fixed-budget advantage came from shorter calls purchasing more delta.

discoveries.headline: The maturity ranking is below the model's resolution.
discoveries.notice: The observed return difference is smaller than the CAGR effect of one volatility point of option-pricing error.
discoveries.lesson: Stop optimizing maturity and test option pricing instead.

sma_rotation.title: 200-day leverage rotation
sma_rotation.thesis: Use a robust trend state primarily to vary leverage intensity rather than to forecast whether equities should be owned at all.
implicit_bets: Persistent adverse regimes can be identified soon enough to reduce destructive leverage
Whipsaw and execution costs do not consume the leverage-timing benefit
Future crashes are not dominated by instantaneous reversals that defeat the signal
does_not_require: Exiting equities completely below the moving average

questions.prompt: Is the moving average forecasting equity returns, or mainly identifying times when high leverage is poorly compensated?
questions.answer_hint: Compare leveraged-to-1x with leveraged-to-T-bill rules. The repo generally found the 1x risk-off state more robust for long-run wealth.

questions.prompt: How much of the apparent edge comes from a few crash sessions?
questions.answer_hint: Measure concentration against both always-on leverage and the 1x index; concentration is pair-dependent.

questions.prompt: Would a retail investor still capture the result after the signal is observable and the trade is executable?
questions.answer_hint: Treat LAG1 and LAG2 as implementation bounds unless a next-open reconstruction is available.

questions.prompt: Does the result survive a broad 150-250 day window, or depend on exactly 200 days?
questions.answer_hint: A broad plateau is more persuasive than a sharp optimum.

questions.prompt: What happens when the market falls quickly and reverses before the signal can re-enter leverage?
questions.answer_hint: This is a characteristic path risk for trend-based leverage control.

discoveries.headline: The signal may be timing leverage more than equities.
discoveries.notice: Remaining in 1x equities below the SMA can preserve long-run compounding better than moving fully to cash.
discoveries.lesson: Frame the SMA as a leverage-state indicator, not necessarily a market-in-or-out predictor.

discoveries.headline: The exact 200-day value is probably not the thesis.
discoveries.notice: A broad window of similar results suggests regime detection rather than parameter magic.
discoveries.lesson: Favor parsimonious robustness over optimizing the moving-average length.

always_on_leverage.title: Always-on leveraged equity
always_on_leverage.thesis: Exchange higher equity exposure for greater volatility drag, financing cost, and crash sensitivity. Long-run success depends on the interaction between arithmetic return and the path of returns.
implicit_bets: The equity risk premium is high enough to overcome volatility drag
The investor survives severe drawdowns without forced selling

questions.prompt: Why can 3x daily exposure produce far less than 3x long-run return?
questions.answer_hint: Separate arithmetic leverage from volatility drag and financing.

questions.prompt: Which matters more here: a lower average equity return or a more volatile path?
questions.answer_hint: Map geometric wealth across both dimensions rather than changing one assumption in isolation.

questions.prompt: How large can the drawdown become before the strategy is behaviorally or financially unholdable?
questions.answer_hint: A strategy that survives mathematically can still fail if the investor cannot remain invested.

stock_bond_leverage.title: Leveraged stock-bond portfolios
stock_bond_leverage.thesis: Combine risky assets whose diversification can permit higher total exposure. The central risk is that the historical equity-bond hedge relationship changes when inflation and rates dominate both legs.
implicit_bets: Equities and duration do not remain positively correlated during the worst periods
Bond carry and convexity compensate for financing and duration risk
Rebalancing retains enough diversification benefit to justify leverage

questions.prompt: What if the hedge asset falls at the same time as equities?
questions.answer_hint: Use 2022 as a direct falsification case rather than relying on average historical correlation.

questions.prompt: Does the bond sleeve diversify risk, or merely look large by capital weight?
questions.answer_hint: Compare duration and volatility contribution, not just portfolio percentages.

questions.prompt: Does adding Treasury leverage improve the lower tail or simply increase gross exposure?
questions.answer_hint: The repo found only modest Treasury leverage attractive in some cells; larger leverage often reduced p5 outcomes.

ui_copy.stop_copy: This difference is smaller than the uncertainty in the model assumption that drives it. Stop tuning this parameter and test the larger uncertainty instead.
